title: Modi Embarks on Six-Day Energy and Trade Blitz Across Five Nations
excerpt: From Abu Dhabi to Rome, PM Modi races to secure India's energy supply and lock in landmark EU trade terms amid Middle East crisis.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi departs on May 15 for a six-day, five-nation sprint covering the UAE, the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and Italy — India's most ambitious diplomatic push to Europe in years. The tour lands at a moment of acute pressure: conflict in West Asia has disrupted global oil flows and strained India's foreign exchange reserves, forcing New Delhi to move fast.

**Energy first, Abu Dhabi:**
Modi lands in Abu Dhabi for talks with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, focusing on energy security, investment, and the welfare of the 4.5 million-strong Indian community living in the Emirates. The stakes are steep — the UAE supplied nearly 11 percent of India's crude last year and meets roughly 40 percent of India's LPG needs, making it an irreplaceable energy partner.

**Tech and trade across Europe:**
In the Netherlands, the agenda centres on semiconductors and AI — India has long coveted access to chip-making equipment from Dutch giant ASML, and this visit is expected to unlock outcomes in advanced manufacturing. Sweden and Norway bring Modi to the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in Oslo, his first-ever visit to Norway and the first Indian prime ministerial trip there in 43 years. The Nordic leg will sharpen cooperation on green hydrogen, emerging technologies, and resilient supply chains. Italy closes the tour, with talks on defence co-production and accelerating the India-EU Free Trade Agreement — announced in January 2026 and expected to take effect in early 2027.

**What to watch:**
Track whether Modi secures concrete energy supply commitments from Abu Dhabi and whether ASML access moves from aspiration to signed agreement in The Hague.
